one_line.text: Computer scientist and non-fiction author who studies distributed systems academically and writes for general readers about attention, technology, work, and productivity.

biography.text: Newport is a full professor of computer science at Georgetown University. He earned his doctorate at MIT and researches the theory of distributed systems, especially what can and cannot be solved under difficult communication conditions. Alongside that technical career, he has written books and essays about study, skill, digital tools, communication overload, and meaningful work.

background.text: His productivity framework grew from academic research and writing, where long self-directed blocks can produce papers, proofs, and books. He began writing study advice for students, then moved into career capital, focused work, deliberate technology use, email overload, and sustainable output. Deep Work was written partly to explain and systematise how he protected concentration in his own career.

expertise.text: Newport has direct expertise in computer science, academic research, writing, and the personal practice of focused knowledge work. He is an experienced synthesiser of work habits and digital culture rather than an experimental psychologist, neuroscientist, occupational-health researcher, or representative sample of all occupations.

perspective_and_limits.text: His strongest lens is the autonomous maker: someone judged mainly by difficult artefacts and able to control at least part of a schedule. He does acknowledge executives, sales, lobbying, and other communication-heavy exceptions, but the examples and techniques remain easiest for academics, writers, programmers, students, and independent creators. Applying them to care, service, management, operations, disability, or precarious work requires organisational changes and adaptation, not more individual discipline alone.

selected_works.title: Deep Work
selected_works.relationship: Defines concentrated, demanding work as a trainable capability and offers four rules for protecting it.

selected_works.title: Digital Minimalism
selected_works.relationship: Extends selective tool use from professional focus to personal digital life.

selected_works.title: A World Without Email
selected_works.relationship: Moves from personal focus tactics to redesigning organisational communication and workflow.

selected_works.title: Slow Productivity
selected_works.relationship: Develops a more sustainable philosophy of doing fewer things, working at a natural pace, and prioritising quality.
